format.file: {format, spec, cases: [case]}; every case runs on its own, from an empty engine.
format.case: name, why (what the case shows), clock, dev_bounds, groups, labels, tokens, pools, events, expect, expect_state.
format.clock: Clock(ms_per_slot): the measured ms per slot by epoch, keys are epoch numbers as strings (the store meta's ms_per_slot), values verbatim floats: parse them bit-exact (serde_json float_roundtrip). An epoch not in the map takes the last earlier one, else 267.3 (strategies.py:57-66).
format.dev_bounds: [lo, hi): Engine(dev_bounds=...), as the store's meta_bounds; burn = dlo = lo + slots(ms(324000), lo), dhi = hi - slots(ms(20000), hi - 1) (engine.py:250-253).
format.groups: the exact text the engine journals as state 'groups' (engine.py:1386-1391, groups_state: json.dumps with sort_keys of name -> primary, variants, farm, segments, d, d_ms, q, n2_k, risk, wallet, require_farm_complete). The engine is built from it with ignore_risk: every group passes its risk limits (engine.py:532-535).
format.labels: address -> a readable name, for the case's synthetic keys and traders (documentation only).
format.tokens: the mints table: mint, create_slot, creator, mayhem, quote_mint; null is None (a quote_mint of None is never SOL). A curve key that is not listed is an absent mint.
format.pools: the pools table after COALESCE(mint, pool), as snapshot pools.parquet and ReplayFeed have it: pool, mint, orientation (normal or reversed), quote_class, mayhem, coin_creator, create_slot. The engine knows only the SOL markets, quote_class sol or reversed (feed.py:97-99); a pool of another class is listed but unknown to it.
format.events: the feed in chain order (slot, tx, outer, inner), one leg each: venue (curve or pool), key (the mint or the pool), slot, tx, outer, inner, block_time (null: None), then the leg's fields for its venue.
format.events.curve: backtest/replay.py CurveLeg as lab/core CurveLeg holds it: variant (as CurveVariant::as_str spells it), is_buy, t, q, fee (fee plus creator fee), vt, vq, rt, rq (the reserves AFTER the trade), fee_bps, creator_bps, trader, budget, max_cost, min_tokens, min_out (null: absent), direct. The reserves before are vt + s*t, vq - s*q, rt + s*t, rq - s*q with s = 1 for a buy and -1 for a sell (streams.py:35-38).
format.events.pool: backtest/replay.py PoolLeg as lab/core PoolLeg holds it: kind (buy, sell, boost, withdraw or deposit), exact_out, base, quote_net, the pool BEFORE the event (b, e, lp_bps, protocol_bps, creator_bps, cashback_bps, virt), e_delta, trader, limit_quote, limit_base, boost_left, direct, lp_amount, lp_supply (null: absent), farmer. After the event e is e + e_delta, b is b + base for a sell or deposit and b - base otherwise (streams.py:56-57, 66).
format.expect: the journal's signals rows after the run, sorted by (family, variant, key, t), in the C1b projection (paper/journal_diff.py signal_row): family, variant, key, t, day, venue, orientation, depth, trigger_trader, farm, pool_seen_slot, farm_window_complete, block_time, d_ms, farm_complete, gate (the farm gate the row stopped at, or 'pass'), then status and reason as the Python engine wrote them. C1b compares all but status and reason: past the farm gates the engine decides entered or busy (C2/C3), where the Rust route writes NULL; a gated row is 'skipped' with the gate as reason on both sides.
format.expect_state: the engine's signal state after the last slot: first_slot; hour (the first slot of the current hour bucket); hour_events, the N2 candidates of the current hour per bucket (curve, pool_normal, pool_reversed) as [key, slot, depth] in insertion order; farm_win, per pool with items, its items in order, each [slot, tx, outer, inner, SOL amount, farmer SOL amount] (the engine's (slot, order, amount, farm) of engine.py:580 with the slot once: order is (slot, tx, outer, inner)); pool_seen, [first slot, last slot] of every pool with an event, a SOL market or not (step 3 sees every pool key, engine.py:393-395), less the pools the 24 h prune has removed (POOL_SEEN_KEEP_MS, engine.py:697-701).
format.integers: every integer is a JSON integer and fits i64 (the largest here, depths near 1.2e16, lie above 2^53); fields Rust holds as u64 are never negative.
format.regenerate: C1B_CASES_REGEN=1 pytest paper/tests/test_signal_cases.py (or python -m paper.tests.c1b_signal_cases): expect and expect_state are the engine's own output.

cases.name: pool_mint_absent
cases.why: Pools need no token: 'mint absent' is for curves only (spec §3.5). PA (reversed, no token) signals, its creator being its coin_creator. PB (reversed, no token): its coin_creator's sell 100 slots before the trigger blocks it, as the creator's would. PC (sol, token present, creator TC): its coin_creator's sell does not block, the token's creator wins. PD (sol, token present with creator NULL): creator is None, no fallback to coin_creator, so its coin_creator's sell does not block either.

cases.name: n2_band_edges_above_2_53
cases.why: The pool band compares an integer depth with 0.8 and 1.2 times the trigger's depth exactly (spec D7). P's depth is 12,000,000,000,000,000, so the band is [9,600,000,000,000,000, 14,400,000,000,000,000], both above 2^53. E_lo and E_hi lie on the edges and are picked (k = 3); X_lo (one below) and X_hi (one above) are not, although as f64 they round onto the edges (a cast to f64 would take them).

cases.name: n2_curve_universe
cases.why: The curve N2 universe is every non-mayhem SOL-quoted token, of any age (engine.py:702-705), in the band of +-5 SOL around the trigger's depth, both edges included. CT triggers (k = 3): C_hi (quote 1111, depth +5 SOL), C_lo (WSOL, -5 SOL) and C_old (created before burn) are picked; C_hi_out (+5 SOL + 1), C_lo_out (-5 SOL - 1), C_qnull (quote None), C_mayhem, C_pump (quote PUMP) and C_absent (no token) are not. C_old's own trigger after CT gives no row: its curve is older than burn.

cases.name: n2_collision
cases.why: Two triggers in one slot pick the same N2 key, and the later write wins (INSERT OR REPLACE, spec §3.9). In slot S, P1 (depth 850 SOL, farm flagged: its farmers made 6 of its 7 SOL in the hour) and then P2 (1,180 SOL, organic) both have only Q (1,000 SOL) in their band. Q's N2 row carries P2's depth and farm; the Python engine wrote it as busy, after P1's write entered it (status is C2's).

cases.name: hour_rollover_order
cases.why: The hour rolls over inside a slot, after its first key's F7 (engine.py:403-406, 689). Slot B = 450179413 opens an hour (h 13,441 at epoch 1042). P1 (950 SOL), B's first key, triggers and still sees the previous hour: its N2 picks Q (1,000 SOL) and P2 (1,048 SOL at its inflow, B - 30). P2 (1,050 SOL) triggers next in B and sees only the new hour, where P1 is: it picks P1, not Q (k = 3).

cases.name: clock_1041_1042_mid_hour
cases.why: At the epoch change 450144000 the hour grid moves: h is 13,542 slots in 1041 (bucket 450136080) and 13,441 in 1042 (bucket 450139090), so the first event slot at or after 450144000 starts a new hour in the middle of the old one. Q trades at 450143800. P1 triggers at 450144010 as that slot's first key and still sees the old bucket: its N2 picks Q. P2 triggers at 450144100 and sees only the new bucket: it picks P1, not Q (k = 3), where with the 1041 clock throughout it would still see Q.

cases.name: h_gates
cases.why: Group H's gates, in the engine's order (engine.py:737-742). The feed starts at t0 = 450190000 (O trades), so farm_window_complete is 1 from t0 + 13,441 on (one hour at epoch 1042). PW triggers at t0 + 5,000: H skips it with 'farm window incomplete'. PE0 at t0 + 13,440 is incomplete too, PE1 at t0 + 13,441 complete. PF's and PFW's farmers made more than half of their SOL volume in the hour before: farm 'flagged'. PFW triggers at t0 + 5,500, its window incomplete: H skips it with 'farm flagged', the gate it checks first. PF (window complete) is skipped with 'farm flagged' too. PO is organic with a complete window: H passes it. K3 (farm all) passes every one.
